FormFieldRuleCdu.description: One declared field of a  {@link  FormCduProps } : where it lives and how it validates.

props.description:
CDU props for `Form` — the host-form bridge. This catalog does NOT register it: the renderer ships it (`formPrimitive`, `cdu-renderer/src/forms/Form.primitive.tsx`) and `cdu-harness` `buildRegistry` adds it next to the catalog, so every host renders it.

Its contract lives here because this is what the save-time validators read — sim-api (`internal/cdu/catalog`, synced by `make sync-cdu-schema`) and the smart-form editor. Without it a stored page could not hold a `Form`, and `form.submit` would send the process an empty `formData` (the values live under `vm[valueKey]`, read through the Form).

Mirrors the Zod `props` of `Form.primitive.tsx`; `cdu-harness` asserts the two agree.

anyOf.description: Field rules driving `form.validate` (`vm.errors[valueKey]` / `vm.valid[valueKey]`).

valueKey.description: The vm key holding this form's values (default: the form id). Values live at `vm[valueKey]`.

Booleanish.description: Used to represent DOM API's where users can either pass true or false as a boolean or as its equivalent strings.

LayoutElement.description:
Elements a layout primitive may render.

A closed union rather than full polymorphism: it keeps props inferable, keeps the primitive's own recipe valid (every member is a block-level container), and rules out `as="button"`-style abuse of a layout box as a control.

LayoutLayer.description: Stacking layer for a layered layout child: `back` (behind everything, e.g. a background), `base` (normal content), `dock` (above content, e.g. a dock).

LayoutReveal.description: When a layout child is shown: `hover` hides it until the nearest `hoverScope` ancestor is hovered or focused (always shown on coarse pointers); `always` is the plain default.

PaddingSide.description: A side (or axis) that padding may be applied to. `x` = left + right, `y` = top + bottom. Used by the `sides` prop of the layout primitives.

aria-activedescendant.description: Identifies the currently active element when DOM focus is on a composite widget, textbox, group, or application.

anyOf.description: Indicates whether assistive technologies will present all, or only parts of, the changed region based on the change notifications defined by the aria-relevant attribute.
Indicates whether inputting text could trigger display of one or more predictions of the user's intended value for an input and specifies how predictions would be presented if they are made.

aria-braillelabel.description: Defines a string value that labels the current element, which is intended to be converted into Braille.

aria-brailleroledescription.description: Defines a human-readable, author-localized abbreviated description for the role of an element, which is intended to be converted into Braille.

anyOf.description: Indicates the current "checked" state of checkboxes, radio buttons, and other widgets.
Defines the total number of columns in a table, grid, or treegrid.
Defines an element's column index or position with respect to the total number of columns within a table, grid, or treegrid.

aria-colindextext.description: Defines a human readable text alternative of aria-colindex.

anyOf.description: Defines the number of columns spanned by a cell or gridcell within a table, grid, or treegrid.

aria-controls.description: Identifies the element (or elements) whose contents or presence are controlled by the current element.

anyOf.description: Indicates the element that represents the current item within a container or set of related elements.

aria-describedby.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.

aria-description.description: Defines a string value that describes or annotates the current element.

aria-details.description: Identifies the element that provides a detailed, extended description for the object.

anyOf.description: Indicates that the element is perceivable but disabled, so it is not editable or otherwise operable.
Indicates what functions can be performed when a dragged object is released on the drop target.

aria-errormessage.description: Identifies the element that provides an error message for the object.

anyOf.description: Indicates whether the element, or another grouping element it controls, is currently expanded or collapsed.

aria-flowto.description: Identifies the next element (or elements) in an alternate reading order of content which, at the user's discretion, allows assistive technology to override the general default of reading in document source order.

anyOf.description: Indicates an element's "grabbed" state in a drag-and-drop operation.
Indicates the availability and type of interactive popup element, such as menu or dialog, that can be triggered by an element.
Indicates whether the element is exposed to an accessibility API.
Indicates the entered value does not conform to the format expected by the application.

aria-keyshortcuts.description: Indicates keyboard shortcuts that an author has implemented to activate or give focus to an element.

aria-label.description: Defines a string value that labels the current element.

aria-labelledby.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

anyOf.description: Defines the hierarchical level of an element within a structure.
Indicates that an element will be updated, and describes the types of updates the user agents, assistive technologies, and user can expect from the live region.
Indicates whether an element is modal when displayed.
Indicates whether a text box accepts multiple lines of input or only a single line.
Indicates that the user may select more than one item from the current selectable descendants.
Indicates whether the element's orientation is horizontal, vertical, or unknown/ambiguous.

aria-owns.description: Identifies an element (or elements) in order to define a visual, functional, or contextual parent/child relationship between DOM elements where the DOM hierarchy cannot be used to represent the relationship.

aria-placeholder.description: Defines a short hint (a word or short phrase) intended to aid the user with data entry when the control has no value. A hint could be a sample value or a brief description of the expected format.

anyOf.description: Defines an element's number or position in the current set of listitems or treeitems. Not required if all elements in the set are present in the DOM.
Indicates the current "pressed" state of toggle buttons.
Indicates that the element is not editable, but is otherwise operable.
Indicates what notifications the user agent will trigger when the accessibility tree within a live region is modified.
Indicates that user input is required on the element before a form may be submitted.

aria-roledescription.description: Defines a human-readable, author-localized description for the role of an element.

anyOf.description: Defines the total number of rows in a table, grid, or treegrid.
Defines an element's row index or position with respect to the total number of rows within a table, grid, or treegrid.

aria-rowindextext.description: Defines a human readable text alternative of aria-rowindex.

anyOf.description: Defines the number of rows spanned by a cell or gridcell within a table, grid, or treegrid.
Indicates the current "selected" state of various widgets.
Defines the number of items in the current set of listitems or treeitems. Not required if all elements in the set are present in the DOM.
Indicates if items in a table or grid are sorted in ascending or descending order.
Defines the maximum allowed value for a range widget.
Defines the minimum allowed value for a range widget.
Defines the current value for a range widget.

aria-valuetext.description: Defines the human readable text alternative of aria-valuenow for a range widget.

anyOf.description:
Element to render instead of a `div`. Use it to give a region correct semantics (`ul` for a navigator, `nav`/`aside`/`header` for landmarks) without dropping to a raw element.

List elements (`ul`/`ol`/`li`) render with their browser bullet, margin and indent removed — the primitive stays a pure layout box.

Paint the region with a semantic surface token (e.g. `'surfaceMuted'`, `'surfaceSubtle'`, `'background'`). The typed, sanctioned form of the `style={{ background: token }}` escape hatch — use it to give a layout region a surface without wrapping it in a Card. Colour only: text colour stays on the children (`Label color`), and borders/radius belong to Card.

Whether to apply padding to the bottom side.

⚠️ See  {@link  left }  — setting one side turns the unspecified ones off. Prefer  {@link  sides } .

Custom padding sizes for each side using CSS-like syntax
- 1 value: all sides
- 2 values: [vertical, horizontal] = [top/bottom, left/right]
- 3 values: [top, horizontal, bottom] = [top, left/right, bottom]
- 4 values: [top, right, bottom, left]

When customSize is provided, size and directional props (left/right/top/bottom) are ignored
Absolutely fill the nearest `positioned` ancestor (`position: absolute; inset: 0`) — a full-bleed layer such as a background behind content. Pair with `layer` to control stacking order.
Whether the space should take full height
Anchor the element to the full dynamic viewport height (`100dvh`, with a `100vh` fallback). Use on the outermost shell container.
Whether the space should take full width
Grow to fill the free space of a flex parent (`flex: 1 1 0%`).

Make this region the hover scope for its `reveal="hover"` descendants: they appear while it is hovered or holds keyboard focus. Emits `data-hover-scope` on the element — a row, a card, a message bubble whose actions should show on approach rather than compete with the content.
Hints at the type of data that might be entered by the user while editing the element or its contents

is.description: Specify that a standard HTML element should behave like a defined custom built-in element

anyOf.description: Stacking order for layered children: `back` (behind), `base` (content), `dock` (above). No default — z-index is applied only when set.

Whether to apply padding to the left side.

⚠️ Specifying **any** of `left`/`right`/`top`/`bottom` turns every
*unspecified* side **off**. `{ top: false }` therefore means "no padding at all", not "all sides but top". Prefer  {@link  sides } .
Allow shrinking below the content's intrinsic height by setting `min-height: 0`. Required for a nested scroll area inside a flex column.
Allow shrinking below the content's intrinsic width by setting `min-width: 0`. Required to let a flex child truncate its own children (e.g. an ellipsised Label inside a row).
Click event handler

Make the region transparent to the pointer (`pointer-events: none`), so it frames and positions its children without becoming a hit target itself.

For a full-bleed wrapper whose only job is geometry — a centring band over a canvas, an absolutely-positioned overlay column. Children opt back in with `pointerThrough={false}` on the box that should actually receive events.
Establish a positioning context (`position: relative`) so a `fill` child can absolutely fill it. Use on the layered shell container.

`hover` hides this region (`opacity: 0; pointer-events: none`) until the nearest `hoverScope` ancestor is hovered or focused, or the region itself takes focus — so a keyboard user always reaches it. Where any pointer is coarse (`(any-pointer: coarse)`) it is always shown: touch cannot hover, and a hidden action there would be an invisible tap target. Opacity only — the content stays mounted and in the tab order. `always` is the default.

Whether to apply padding to the right side.

⚠️ See  {@link  left }  — setting one side turns the unspecified ones off. Prefer  {@link  sides } .
Make the element scroll its overflow (`overflow: auto`) and shrink as a flex child (`min-width/height: 0`), so a scroll region "just works" without the usual min-size incantation.
Scrollbar appearance. Only meaningful together with `scroll`.

Elevation for a layout region, from the `boxShadow` token scale — the typed form of `style={{ boxShadow: token }}`.

Card owns elevation for a *surface* (it also brings a border and a radius). This is for a region that is only a band or a plane: a docked chrome bar separated from the content it floats over, where a Card's border and radius would be wrong. Shadow only — background stays with  {@link  background } .

Whether this element may shrink below its content size as a flex child. `false` pins it (`flex-shrink: 0`) so a neighbouring `grow` region absorbs the deficit instead. Defaults to `true` (the flexbox default).

The sides to pad, listed explicitly. `'x'` = left + right, `'y'` = top + bottom. Wins over `left`/`right`/`top`/`bottom`, and is the recommended form: it says what it means and has no interaction between props.
Padding size

Stick to the top of the nearest scroll container (`position: sticky; top: 0`). Use for section headers inside a `scroll` region. The element must carry its own background so scrolled content does not show through.
Stick to the bottom of the nearest scroll container (`position: sticky; bottom: 0`). Mirror of `sticky` for a bottom-anchored dock.

Whether to apply padding to the top side.

⚠️ See  {@link  left }  — setting one side turns the unspecified ones off. Prefer  {@link  sides } .

ScrollStyle.description:
Scrollbar appearance for a scrollable layout primitive. A CLOSED set — apps pick a design-system look, never raw scrollbar CSS.
- `native` — the platform scrollbar (default)
- `thin` — slim, theme-tinted bar (semantic `border` colour)
- `hidden` — scrolling works, the bar is not painted

props.description:
CDU props for `Stack` — the serializable, authorable subset made of Stack's
**own** declared props plus the inherited `LayoutBehaviorProps` flex knobs. Layout primitive: children come from the tree node's `children`, not props; `id`/`className`/`ref` are the renderer's.

Deliberately excluded:
- `divider` — `ReactNode`, not serializable (could later be a slot).

`space` is Stack's nested padding config (`SpaceConfig`).
